title: Iridescent Lamp & Enchanted Mug Material Workshop
description: A cozy desk scene where an iridescent lamp illuminates a coffee mug. The user acts as a material designer, adjusting the mug's physical material properties (metalness, roughness, color, emissive glow, opacity, and environment map intensity) through an interactive panel while the lamp casts dynamic iridescent light that reveals how each parameter interacts with the lighting.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads IridescenceLamp.glb and coffeeMug.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: place the coffee mug at the origin on a subtle circular platform (dark wood-textured MeshStandardMaterial plane, radius 2). Position the iridescent lamp to the left and slightly behind the mug (x:-1.5, y:0, z:-0.5) so it appears to illuminate the mug. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2.5, 4) looking at (0, 0.8, 0) with OrbitControls enabled (damping on, min/max distance 2-8). Lighting: add a warm PointLight (color 0xffeedd, intensity 3) parented near the lamp's bulb area to simulate the lamp casting light. Add a subtle AmbientLight (0x222233, intensity 0.3) and an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a simple RoomEnvironment from three/addons. Core interaction: build an HTML/CSS panel (top-right, semi-transparent dark background, rounded corners) with 6 labeled sliders: (1) Metalness 0-1 default 0.1, (2) Roughness 0-1 default 0.5, (3) Color via hue slider 0-360 mapped to HSL, (4) Emissive Intensity 0-2 default 0, (5) Opacity 0.1-1 default 1 (enable material.transparent when <1), (6) Env Map Intensity 0-3 default 1. On load, traverse the coffeeMug model and collect all Mesh children. Replace their materials with a single shared MeshPhysicalMaterial. Each slider input event updates the corresponding property on this shared material in real-time. Add a 'Randomize' button that animates all 6 parameters to random valid values over 0.5 seconds using GSAP-style lerp in the render loop. Add a 'Reset' button restoring defaults. Validate all parameters stay within defined min/max ranges on every update. The lamp should slowly rotate its iridescent shade (rotate y by 0.003 per frame) to create shifting light reflections on the mug. Display current numeric values next to each slider. Render with tone mapping (ACESFilmic) and outputColorSpace sRGB. The animation loop should run continuously with requestAnimationFrame.
